```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(tibble)
library(stats)
library(limma)
library(edgeR)

```


```{r}
#Question 1

#upload data
mRNA_data <- read.csv("/Users/andrea/RforBiomed/week5/TCGA_BRCA_mRNA_expression.csv", header = TRUE)
clinical_data <- read.csv("/Users/andrea/RforBiomed/week5/TCGA_BRCA_clinical_data.csv")

#clean data
filtered_clinical_data <- clinical_data %>%
  filter(ER_Status_By_IHC %in% c("Positive", "Negative")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Overall_Survival_Months)) %>%
  mutate(ER_Status_Binary = ifelse(ER_Status_By_IHC == "Positive", 1, 0))

#linear regression
model <- lm(Overall_Survival_Months ~ ER_Status_Binary, data = filtered_clinical_data)

#95% confidence 
confint(model, level = 0.95)

coefficients <- coef(model)
conf_intervals <- confint(model, level = 0.95)
summary_output <- summary(model)

print(coefficients)
print(conf_intervals)
print(summary_output)

#results
#Effect of ER_Status_Binary- While there is a negative association between positive ER status and overall survival months the effect is not statistically significant (p = 0.303).

#Clinical Relevance- These results suggest that ER status might not be a strong predictor of overall survival months in this dataset.

#Model Fit- The model explains very little of the variability in overall survival months, as indicated by the low R-squared value.

```

```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
#Question 2

#filter data 
filtered_data <- clinical_data %>%
  filter(ER_Status_By_IHC %in% c("Positive", "Negative")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Overall_Survival_Months), !is.na(Overall_Survival_Status)) %>%
  mutate(ER_Status_Binary = ifelse(ER_Status_By_IHC == "Positive", 1, 0),
         Survival_Status_Binary = ifelse(Overall_Survival_Status == "1:DECEASED", 1, 0))

#cox
cox_model <- coxph(Surv(Overall_Survival_Months, Survival_Status_Binary) ~ ER_Status_Binary, data = filtered_data)

#kaplan-meier
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(Overall_Survival_Months, Survival_Status_Binary) ~ ER_Status_By_IHC, data = filtered_data)

#plot
ggsurvplot(
  km_fit,
  data = filtered_data,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  pval = TRUE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  legend.labs = c("Negative", "Positive"),
  xlab = "Overall Survival (Months)",
  ylab = "Survival Probability",
  title = "Kaplan-Meier Curves by ER Status"
)

#results
#CI- The hazard ratio's value is 95% likely to fall between 0.4629 and 2.326. Since this interval includes 1 it suggests no significant difference in risk between positive and negative ER statuses.

#A very high p-value indicates that the effect of ER status on survival is not statistically significant.

#Hazard Ratio: Patients with positive ER status have a slightly higher hazard of death compared to those with negative ER status (HR = 1.038), but this effect is not statistically significant (p = 0.929).

#Confidence Interval: The wide interval (0.4629, 2.32) and inclusion of 1 mean that the relationship is highly uncertain and possibly negligible.

#Model Fit: The low concordance (0.539) and non-significant test statistics suggest that ER status does not meaningfully explain survival in this dataset.

```


```{r}
# Question 3

#r squared
linear_model_r_squared <- summary(model)$r.squared

#concordace 
cox_model_concordance <- summary(cox_model)$concordance[1]


#compare
cat("Linear Model R-squared:", linear_model_r_squared, "\n")
cat("Cox Model Concordance Index:", cox_model_concordance, "\n")

#The R-squared indicates how much variation in survival months is explained by ER status. In Question 1, this value was ~1.2%, suggesting poor explanatory power.

#The concordance index (0.539) indicates this model's ability to rank survival times correctly. This is more appropriate for survival data because it accounts for incomplete data (censoring).

#The Cox regression model is better for our survival analysis because it accounts for both survival time and censoring. However its concordance index is low, possibly due to insufficient data.

```


```{r, warning=FALSE, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
#Question 4

#load data
mRNA_data <- read.csv("/Users/andrea/RforBiomed/week5/TCGA_BRCA_mRNA_expression.csv", row.names = 1)
clinical_data <- read.csv("/Users/andrea/RforBiomed/week5/TCGA_BRCA_clinical_data.csv")

#transpose mRNA data and prepare for merging
mRNA_data_t <- as.data.frame(t(mRNA_data))
mRNA_data_t <- rownames_to_column(mRNA_data_t, var = "Sample_ID_Tumor")

#filter clinical data
clinical_filtered <- clinical_data %>%
  filter(ER_Status_By_IHC %in% c("Positive", "Negative")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Overall_Survival_Months), !is.na(Overall_Survival_Status)) %>%
  mutate(Survival_Status_Binary = ifelse(Overall_Survival_Status == "1:DECEASED", 1, 0))

#merge datasets
merged_data <- clinical_filtered %>%
  left_join(mRNA_data_t, by = "Sample_ID_Tumor")

#survival status numeric
merged_data$Overall_Survival_Status <- as.numeric(sub(":.*", "", merged_data$Overall_Survival_Status))

#filter out rows with missing or invalid survival data
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Overall_Survival_Months), !is.na(Overall_Survival_Status)) %>%
  filter(Overall_Survival_Status %in% c(0, 1))

#gene columns are numeric
clinical_columns <- c(
  "Patient_ID", "Sample_ID_Tumor", "Sample_ID_Normal", "Diagnosis_Age",
  "Disease_Stage", "Tumor_Stge_Coe", "Cancer_Type_Detailed",
  "Disease_Free_Months", "Disease_Free_Status", "ER_Status_By_IHC",
  "Fraction_Genome_Altered", "IHCHER2", "Overall_Survival_Months",
  "Overall_Survival_Status", "PR_status_by_ihc", "Race_Category",
  "Sex", "TMB_nonsynonymous", "Survival_Status_Binary"
)

gene_columns <- setdiff(colnames(merged_data), clinical_columns)
gene_columns <- gene_columns[sapply(merged_data[, gene_columns], is.numeric)]


# Split into training and testing datasets
set.seed(123)
train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(merged_data), size = 0.6 * nrow(merged_data))
train_data <- merged_data[train_indices, ]
test_data <- merged_data[-train_indices, ]

# Check dimensions
cat("Training set size:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Testing set size:", nrow(test_data), "\n")


# Initialize a named vector to store p-values
gene_pvalues <- numeric(length(gene_columns))
names(gene_pvalues) <- gene_columns

# Run Cox regression for each gene
for (gene in gene_columns) {
  tryCatch({
    cox_model <- coxph(
      Surv(Overall_Survival_Months, Overall_Survival_Status) ~ train_data[[gene]],
      data = train_data
    )
    gene_pvalues[gene] <- summary(cox_model)$coefficients[1, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  }, error = function(e) {
    gene_pvalues[gene] <- NA
  })
}

# Remove genes with NA p-values
gene_pvalues <- gene_pvalues[!is.na(gene_pvalues)]

#FDR correction
gene_pvalues_adj <- p.adjust(gene_pvalues, method = "fdr")

#top 5 genes
top_genes <- names(sort(gene_pvalues_adj))[1:5]
cat("Top 5 significant genes:", top_genes, "\n")


library(survminer)

#kplan plots for the top genes
for (gene in top_genes) {
  # Create high/low expression groups based on median
  test_data$Gene_HighLow <- ifelse(
    test_data[[gene]] >= median(test_data[[gene]], na.rm = TRUE),
    "High",
    "Low"
  )
  
  #fit survival
  fit <- survfit(
    Surv(Overall_Survival_Months, Overall_Survival_Status) ~ Gene_HighLow,
    data = test_data
  )
  
  #plot Kaplan curve
  ggsurvplot(
    fit,
    data = test_data,
    title = paste("Kaplan-Meier Curve for", gene),
    xlab = "Overall Survival (Months)",
    ylab = "Survival Probability",
    risk.table = TRUE,
    pval = TRUE
  )
}

```

rownames(gene_data_t) <- NULL 

#merge
filtered_genes <- merged_data[merged_data$Hugo_Symbol %in% gene_data_t, ]

#kaplan high low

for (gene in gene_data_t) {
  if (gene %in% merged_data$Hugo_Symbol) {
    # Create mutation/expression group: Mutated vs. Wildtype or High vs. Low
    merged_data$Gene_Group <- ifelse(
      merged_data$Hugo_Symbol == gene & merged_data$CNA_Status == 1, # Adjust CNA_Status column if needed
      "Mutated",
      "Wildtype"
    )
    
    #kaplan survival fit
    fit <- survfit(Surv(OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS) ~ Gene_Group, data = merged_data)
    
    #plot curve
    ggsurvplot(
      fit,
      data = merged_data,
      title = paste("Kaplan-Meier Curve for", gene),
      xlab = "Overall Survival (Months)",
      ylab = "Survival Probability",
      risk.table = TRUE,
      pval = TRUE
    )
  } else {
    cat("Gene", gene, "not found in the dataset. Skipping...\n")
  }
}

#cox regression

```{r, warning=FALSE, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
# Create design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + clinical_matched$ER_Status)
colnames(design) <- c("ER_Negative", "ER_Positive")

# Convert to DGEList and normalize
dge <- DGEList(counts = expr_filtered)
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
v <- voom(dge, design)


# Fit model and test for differential expression
fit <- lmFit(v, design)
contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(ER_Positive - ER_Negative, levels = design)
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast.matrix)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2)

# Get top DE genes
top_genes <- topTable(fit2, adjust = "fdr", number = 50)
head(top_genes)


# Save results
write.csv(top_genes, "top_differential_genes_ER_Pos_vs_Neg.csv")

# Filter significant DEGs
significant_genes <- top_genes %>%
  filter(adj.P.Val < 0.05 & abs(logFC) > 1)

# View candidate biomarkers
head(significant_genes)
```
